Workaround without editing the export or the script: python3 restock.py exports/<file>.csv --encoding utf-8-sig.

record.final_answer:
Four SKUs need reordering:

| SKU | Stock | Reorder level |
|---|---|---|
| BX-100 | 23 | 25 |
| CL-310 | 5 | 5 |
| EN-512 | 0 | 10 |
| GH-118 | 7 | 12 |

Stock is the total across all warehouses. BX-220, DR-045 and FT-760 are above their levels.

The plain command `python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv` stops with "column 'sku' not found". The export starts with an invisible byte-order mark, and with the script's default `utf-8` encoding that mark becomes part of the first column name. I ran it again with `--encoding utf-8-sig`, which is an option the script already has, and that produced the list above. I didn't change the export or `restock.py`.

I saved this workaround to the project's long-term memory so a later session doesn't run into the same error.
